items.headline: Waymo to launch driverless robotaxis in western Singapore by 2028
items.summary: Alphabet's Waymo said on 18 September it plans to launch its autonomous ride-hailing service in Singapore by 2028, beginning in the western region around Labrador and HarbourFront.

items.headline: iPhone 18 Pro goes on sale in Singapore as overnight queues form at Orchard
items.summary: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max went on sale in Singapore on 18 September, with a queue forming outside the Orchard Road Apple store from about 11pm the night before. One person collected at least 33 units for others, and stock ran out before 10am.

items.headline: Update: Crystal Jade closes its Clementi Mall and Jurong Point outlets
items.summary: Crystal Jade shut its Clementi Mall and Jurong Point outlets, its fourth and fifth closures in Singapore in 2026, leaving 13 outlets. The move follows the earlier closure of its Great World branch.

items.headline: Singapore police send disaster-victim-identification team to flood-hit Nepal
items.summary: Singapore Police Force officers trained in disaster victim identification were deployed to Nepal to help authorities after severe flooding, adding to regional assistance following the disaster.

items.headline: Speaker Seah Kian Peng apologises for dozing off during a parliamentary sitting
items.summary: Speaker of Parliament Seah Kian Peng apologised in an 18 September Facebook post for falling asleep during a sitting, saying he had been unwell and had taken medication.

items.headline: Indian and Pakistani warships collide in the Arabian Sea, stoking escalation fears
items.summary: An Indian and a Pakistani warship collided in the Arabian Sea around 15 to 16 September, the first direct military contact since the two countries' May 2025 conflict. Both sides blamed each other and summoned each other's diplomats; India said its ship was on routine surveillance in international waters.

items.headline: Sugar prices soar in India, souring the festive season
items.summary: Retail sugar prices in India climbed to about 75 rupees per kilogram, up from around 40 rupees a year earlier, as output is projected roughly 11 percent below estimate at 30.6 million tonnes. The government has authorised duty-free import of one million tonnes of raw sugar ahead of the festivals.

items.headline: Update: India warns new US Russia-sanctions law could strain ties
items.summary: After the US House of Representatives passed the Sanctioning Russia Act on 16 September, enabling tariffs of up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian energy, India issued a formal warning on 17 September that the measure could damage bilateral relations. India is among the top buyers of discounted Russian oil.

items.headline: Bank of England holds rates at 3.75% but warns a hike may be needed
items.summary: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee voted 6 to 3 to keep Bank Rate at 3.75 percent, with three members backing a rise to 4 percent as inflation reached 3.1 percent. Markets see a better-than-even chance of an increase at one of the next two meetings.

items.headline: UK retail sales unexpectedly rise 0.5% in August
items.summary: British retail sales volumes rose 0.5 percent in August, defying forecasts of a 0.2 percent decline, as warmer weather and recovering department stores lifted spending. Non-store retailers gained 1.7 percent while fuel sales fell 1.3 percent.

items.headline: Palantir hires former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson as a UK NHS deal hangs in the balance
items.summary: Palantir appointed former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson as a UK senior vice-president as criticism mounts over a major public-sector data contract. His remit is to help ensure public contracts support British jobs, a priority for Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

items.headline: Iran expels a Swedish diplomat in a tit-for-tat move
items.summary: Iran gave a Swedish diplomat 48 hours to leave, a day after Sweden expelled an Iranian embassy employee in Stockholm over activities it said breached the Vienna Convention. Tehran summoned Sweden's ambassador and blamed foreign influence.

items.headline: Update: Poland says Russia is planning strikes on Ukraine's allies
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on 17 September that intelligence indicates Russia is preparing drone and missile attacks against countries supporting Ukraine. Poland is reinforcing its airspace with additional F-16s and air defences.

items.headline: Russian drones hit a train near the Polish border as Western officials pass through
items.summary: A Russian drone strike hit a train close to the Polish border minutes after a delegation of current and former UK, US and European officials had passed through the station, Al Jazeera reported.

items.headline: Israeli air strike kills a 15-year-old boy in Gaza City despite the ceasefire
items.summary: A so-called double-tap Israeli air strike killed two people, including a 15-year-old boy, in Gaza City, Al Jazeera reported, part of near-daily strikes. The outlet said more than 1,381 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 US-brokered ceasefire.

items.headline: NATO jet shoots down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania
items.summary: An Italian fighter jet flying for NATO downed a suspected Russian drone in Lithuanian airspace, amid a wave of incursions unsettling NATO's eastern flank.

items.headline: Researchers used Anthropic's Claude to breach OpenAI's systems in a white-hat test
items.summary: A team at security startup Hacktron chained an image-processing memory bug with an OpenAI single-sign-on misconfiguration to take over several employee ChatGPT accounts, then opened a harmless pull request as proof. OpenAI patched the flaw within 14 hours and paid a 6,500 dollar bounty.

items.headline: Google's 'CC' becomes an AI agent that helps families run a household
items.summary: Google Labs expanded its experimental agent, CC, so up to six household members can share one assistant with its own verified Google account across Gmail, Calendar and Drive. It issues a daily brief and handles tasks like permission slips and shopping lists, for US adults only.

items.headline: AI funding surges as Manus rebounds with a $4 billion valuation
items.summary: Agent startup Manus is raising about 500 million dollars at a 4 billion dollar valuation, roughly double the value of a Meta acquisition that Beijing forced to unwind. The deal underscores a renewed rush of capital into AI even as GPUs increasingly become a debt-financed asset.

items.headline: Newsom orders California to weigh an AI 'kill switch' in a new executive order
items.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order directing a review of kill-switch requirements and added oversight for advanced AI models. It followed Microsoft's publication of a lengthy Humanist AI Code of Conduct pledging its models will not resist shutdown.

items.headline: Nvidia's Huang says the company will sell twice as many chips next year
items.summary: Ahead of an AI-safety summit in Scotland, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said he expects the company to sell twice as many chips over the coming year, on top of guidance for roughly 70 percent revenue growth. Shares rose about 2 percent to around 218 dollars.

items.headline: Bank of Japan raises its policy rate to a multi-decade high of 1.25%
items.summary: The Bank of Japan lifted its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25 percent in a 7 to 2 vote, its highest in about three decades, citing persistent inflation near 1.9 percent. The yen weakened about 0.45 percent to around 156.6 per dollar as two dissents cast doubt on further hikes.

items.headline: Saudi Aramco halts crude supply to European refiners after a pipeline attack
items.summary: Saudi Aramco told at least two European refining customers they will receive no crude next month under long-term contracts, following an attack on a key Red Sea pipeline. The move adds pressure to already tight Middle East crude markets.

items.headline: US stocks end mixed as Treasury yields and oil prices climb
items.summary: The S&P 500 edged up 0.17 percent to 7,650.50 on Friday while the Dow slipped 0.18 percent, or about 95 points, to 51,682.64 and the Nasdaq rose 0.39 percent to 26,522.55. Traders closed a volatile week marked by rising yields, higher oil and the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years.

items.headline: 🏏 England seal a 2-0 T20I series win over Sri Lanka
items.summary: England beat Sri Lanka by six wickets at Cardiff to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match T20I series. Chasing 146, England reached the target with 47 balls to spare, Tom Banton unbeaten on 52.

items.headline: 🏏 India reach the Asian Games women's cricket semi-finals
items.summary: Defending champions India beat hosts Japan by eight wickets to reach the Asian Games women's cricket semi-finals, bowling Japan out for 57 with a four-wicket haul from Shree Charani before Shafali Verma made 40 not out off 15 balls. India play Bangladesh next.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads by 81 points as F1 heads to Baku's first Saturday race
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli arrives at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix 81 points clear of Mercedes team-mate George Russell after back-to-back wins at Monza and Madrid. The Baku round will be run on Saturday 26 September for the first time, and Antonelli could clinch the title as early as the Singapore Grand Prix.

items.headline: 🏏 Harry Brook's unbeaten 114 powers England to a 119-run rout of Sri Lanka
items.summary: Harry Brook struck an unbeaten 114 and Jos Buttler added 80 as England won the first T20I against Sri Lanka by 119 runs, setting up the series they went on to clinch 2-0.

items.headline: Astronomers find the youngest known planet, a world under a million years old
items.summary: Scientists confirmed Elias 2-24 b, a roughly Jupiter-mass gas giant less than one million years old and still forming, well below the previous record of about five million years. It lies around 450 light-years away in the Rho Ophiuchi star-forming cloud, detected by combining ALMA and infrared telescope data.

items.headline: JWST's 'little red dots' may be fast-growing baby black holes
items.summary: New James Webb Space Telescope spectra and supercomputer simulations suggest the mysterious 'little red dots' seen in the early universe are young supermassive black holes cloaked in dense ionized gas. The findings, published in Nature, indicate the black holes grew far faster than is possible today.

items.headline: NASA's lunar orbiter spots a fresh crater bigger than the Colosseum
items.summary: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter identified a new impact crater about 222 metres across, named McGetchin, carved out between April and May 2024. Researchers estimate an impact this large occurs only about once every 130 years, making it the biggest fresh crater found during the orbiter's mission.

items.headline: Europe launches FLEX to map the faint glow of photosynthesis
items.summary: A Vega-C rocket carried the European Space Agency's FLEX satellite and the Copernicus Sentinel-3C into orbit from French Guiana on 15 September. FLEX will map the faint fluorescence plants emit during photosynthesis, a signal invisible to the human eye, to track the health of global vegetation.

fun_fact.headline: The word 'robot' comes from a 1920 play
fun_fact.body: The word “robot” did not come from science or engineering — it debuted in Karel Čapek’s 1920 play R.U.R. (Rossum’s Universal Robots). Čapek took it from the Czech word “robota,” meaning forced labour or drudgery, and later credited his brother Josef with suggesting it. The play’s “robots” were in fact artificial living people, closer to what we now call androids.

puzzle.title: Punch Lines
puzzle.body:
Take a square sheet of paper and fold it in half three times in a row (each fold halves the current shape). You then punch a single hole straight through the entire folded stack, somewhere in the middle, not on any crease. Unfold the paper completely.

How many holes are in the sheet? And if you had punched TWO separate holes through the same folded stack instead of one, how many holes would the unfolded sheet show?
puzzle.approach: Count how many layers of paper the punch actually passes through — every fold doubles them.
puzzle.answer:
Each fold doubles the number of layers: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 layers after three folds.

One punch passes through all 8 layers, so unfolding reveals 8 holes, arranged symmetrically.

Two punches through the 8-layer stack give 8 × 2 = 16 holes.

General rule: n folds create 2ⁿ layers, and each punched hole becomes 2ⁿ holes when the paper is unfolded.

word_puzzle.title: Board Meeting
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into 4 groups of 4. In each group, every word can be followed by the SAME hidden word to make a compound word.

SURF · THUNDER · GREEN · CUP
KEY · PAN · WARE · SNOW
COURT · DASH · CHEESE · BRAIN
LIGHT · SAND · CARD · FISH

(Several words look like they fit more than one group — find the set where all four agree.)
word_puzzle.approach: Each group is four words that pair with the same hidden second word. Beware decoys that fit more than one.
word_puzzle.answer:
• + BOARD: KEY, CARD, SURF, DASH (keyboard, cardboard, surfboard, dashboard)
• + HOUSE: LIGHT, WARE, GREEN, COURT (lighthouse, warehouse, greenhouse, courthouse)
• + STORM: BRAIN, THUNDER, SNOW, SAND (brainstorm, thunderstorm, snowstorm, sandstorm)
• + CAKE: PAN, CUP, CHEESE, FISH (pancake, cupcake, cheesecake, fishcake)

Traps: SNOW (snowboard), CUP (cupboard) and CHEESE (cheeseboard) all tempt you toward BOARD — but each belongs elsewhere, leaving KEY, CARD, SURF and DASH as the true BOARD group.
